keyDemographicFindings: Gender is the strongest demographic predictor of mother-brand preference (chi-sq p=0.016). Female participants choose mother brands at 65.2% vs 53.7% for males — an 11.5 pp gap driven primarily by elevated preference for Corona Sunbrew.
The 21–24 cohort shows the highest mother-brand preference at 75.0%, reflecting young consumers' reliance on globally recognised brand names as cognitive shortcuts in an unfamiliar product category.

Physical activity is one of only two variables reaching statistical significance (p=0.028). Active consumers (4–5 days/week) peak at 66.7%, but Very Active consumers (6–7 days/week) drop to 42.6% — the only demographic segment below 50%.

NA beer experience reduces mother-brand reliance: preference declines from 63.7% among first-time triers to 54.4% among regular consumers, with Brand Trust dropping from 26.7% to 16.2% as experience increases.
Income shows no significant relationship with mother-brand selection (p=0.900) — preference is remarkably stable at 55–63% across the full income spectrum.

Education shows a negative directional relationship (p=0.091): high school or below 67.3% vs graduate degree holders at 53.8%, consistent with higher education correlating with greater brand exploration.
